10 stocks we like better than Cushman & Wakefield ›.

On its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 4, 2026, Cushman & Wakefield (CWK -2.33%) delivered its highest third-quarter revenue in company history. The commercial real estate services firm is turning aggressive debt reduction into lower interest expense while expanding its high-margin services segment, which includes property management and facility operations.

Three key takeaways from management's comments stand out.

Management repaid over $800 million in debt since early 2024, reaching the lowest gross leverage, or total debt relative to earnings, in firm history. Reducing debt lowers ongoing interest costs and increases free cash flow available for operational investments.

In a recent development, by unifying its occupier services unit with property management operations, Cushman & Wakefield streamlined client coverage to capture larger market share. Strategic alignment gives leadership direct access to executive decision-makers managing corporate real estate portfolios.

With debt reduction targets largely complete, management is moving toward a balanced capital allocation model. The company aims to deploy capital into organic expansion across services, leasing, and capital markets transactions while preserving options for disciplined infill acquisitions.

It has been revealed that commercial real estate demand is holding steady across core industrial and high-quality office sectors, and management isn't hiding its satisfaction with current transaction momentum. The firm relies on a broad service platform across geographic regions and deep corporate client relationships to navigate ongoing interest rate moves. Management is watching client property requirements and capital market liquidity.

Long-term value creation depends on turning debt discipline into sustainable fee growth across high-margin business lines.

Latest Update: College Scholarship Breakdown: Types, Sponsors and Eligibility at a Glance

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1371 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nerdwallet

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college.
  • Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding.
  • Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that scholarships have become a standard part of applying for college. You can learn about scholarships in a variety of ways, but looking through an online database of available scholarships — the most common way — can be overwhelming.

Before you go searching for a scholarship, it's important to understand the types of scholarships available and how to identify the ones that give you the best chance of winning, which can save you time and potentially earn you more funding. Here’s what you need to know about scholarships to decide which ones are best for you.

Scholarships are often funded by three groups: private organizations, institutions like universities, and government agencies. None is better than the other when it comes to awarding funds.

Nonprofit organizations and clubs that are looking for students either majoring in or researching certain fields, or who have experience volunteering in a specific field.

Companies that want to support all students or only fund those majoring in a field that relates to the companies’ industries.

Financial institutions, such as banks or credit unions, that want to support their community or their members.

Individuals or families that are funding private scholarships, usually in memory of a loved one.

Universities and colleges that are offering funds to students who attend their campuses.

Research organizations that want to fund students who will research in their areas of interest and further their causes.

In a recent development, these scholarships generally are provided by local, state or federal government agencies for a variety of reasons. Despite being funded by a government agency, the scholarships do not require you to pay back the money — unlike federal student loans.

Some scholarships pay for anything related to college expenses, including tuition, room and board, books and supplies, and more. Other scholarships limit what you can pay for with the funds, such as only tuition or tuition along with books. It’s important to look at this restriction when applying for scholarships to ensure the funds will go toward what you need to cover.

Industry observers note that merit scholarships require you to show excellence or achievements in your schoolwork, through talents and abilities, and even leadership or service work. Because these types of awards can be highly competitive, merit scholarships might require more than just achievements, such as volunteer or leadership experience. This means merit-based scholarships can overlap with other types of scholarship categories. Here are some examples of merit-based scholarships:.

It has been revealed that merit scholarships often require you to have earned a minimum grade point average (GPA). The minimum GPA depends on the scholarship but often ranges from 2.0 to 4.0, with more competitive scholarships usually requiring higher GPAs. Scholarships with lower GPA minimums are more likely to consider additional factors, such as financial need.

Some merit scholarships might require a minimum ACT or SAT score instead of a GPA — or in addition to a minimum GPA.

Merit scholarships might also require applicants to have participated in activities outside of their schoolwork. This is common for scholarships that require membership in a certain group or organization. For example, membership in agricultural clubs, such as 4-H or FFA, and scouting groups, such as the National Eagle Scout Association, appear in scholarship requirements.

Some scholarships emphasize volunteering or community service and only consider applicants who have that experience. Applications vary in how detailed their requirements can be. Some scholarships want only a general description of where and how you’ve volunteered, and others might require experience with a service project that shows more leadership experience or time volunteering with a certain type of organization.

Scholarships that are awarded to students who can’t afford college are called need-based scholarships.

Unmet financial need is the difference between what it will cost you to attend college and what you can afford to pay. Because calculating how much you can afford is a complicated process, many scholarships refer to your FAFSA to document your financial need.

Some scholarship requirements may be as straightforward as demonstrating that you have financial need, but some scholarships might have income limits. However, income restrictions are less common.

It has been revealed that athletic scholarships are for — you guessed it — athletes. They are usually offered by colleges and universities to recruit athletes onto their collegiate teams and can be competitive. Which sports have scholarships available and the scholarship amounts vary by college.

According to recent reports, even though the main criterion for an athletic scholarship is being good at your sport, you’ll likely still need to show that you can keep up with your schoolwork. Most athletic scholarships require students to earn a minimum GPA or test scores to remain eligible while they’re in college.

Some scholarships are designated for students majoring in a general field, such as science or education, but others can be for very specific areas of study. For example, a scholarship for students majoring in a natural resource field could include majors in biology, ecology, wildlife biology, conservation education, forestry, soils and hydrology. However, a stricter scholarship might state that students have to major in more specific topics, such as biochemistry or microbial ecology.

Scholarships are available for active and former members of the military and members of their families. In addition to federal funds available for veterans to attend college, private organizations and some universities have scholarships for veterans to offset the cost of a degree.

According to recent reports, which family members can apply for funds depends on the individual scholarship. For example, some scholarships extend to children or spouses of veterans, but some go as far in a family tree as great-grandchildren.

Veteran- and military-focused scholarships might require that applicants or their family members enlisted in a certain branch, served during a particular time or conflict, or meet a certain rank or status such as receiving disability. Scholarships might also require that the applicant be a wartime veteran or family member of a wartime veteran; not all veterans meet this status.

Scholarships are also awarded to people who identify with a certain group. Common examples of identity-based scholarships include those for people who have disabilities, belong to certain ethnic or religious groups, identify as LGBTQIA+ or are first-generation students. Some identity-based scholarships require applicants to meet several criteria, such as belonging to more than one identity group.

Outside of what would be considered standard DEI groups, there are scholarships for applicants who identify with less common groups, such as veganism, homelessness and model railroad builders.

In a recent development, the best scholarships for you depend on your situation. For example, if you are a skilled athlete with a good academic record, going for an athletic scholarship might give you the most funding. On the other hand, if you’re going to research a topic that isn’t common, looking for scholarships that support your research topic might be your best bet because competition could be lower.

Good tactics to figure out which scholarships are worth your time include:.

Think of the skills, talents, experience and identities that are unique to you. For example, being a child of a veteran immediately qualifies you for scholarships with fewer applicants than scholarships open to everyone. Likewise, if you embrace a certain ethnicity, identify with a specific group or have experience with a type of work, you might qualify for scholarships that appreciate and recognize those attributes more than the average scholarship.

Industry observers note that apply if you think you're eligible. Don’t apply to just a few scholarships and hope you get them. Instead, apply for as many scholarships as you can and for which you’re eligible. This increases your chances of receiving funds. Even small scholarships can make a massive impact when you add several of them together.

Understand how you can use the money. If you already have a scholarship that covers only books, applying for the same type of scholarship isn’t helpful if you don’t need the extra funds. Instead, look for scholarships that cover the costs you have remaining.

Not sure where to look? Our sister site Scholarships360.org provides students with vetted scholarship opportunities. That would be a good place to start.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, global stock markets remain volatile amid persistent geopolitical tensions and concerns about the sustainability of AI trade. Given this backdrop, investors seeking steady income can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios.

    Tracking recommendations from top Wall Street analysts can help investors pick attractive stocks, as these experts assess a company's ability to pay dividends consistently.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Integrated oil and gas giant Chevron (CVX) is a dividend king. The firm has increased its dividend for 39 consecutive years. At a quarterly dividend of $1.78 per share (annualized dividend of $7.12 per share), CVX offers a yield of 3.14%. Chevron will announce its third-quarter results on October 30.

    Sources indicate that in an earnings preview note on U.S. oil majors, Goldman Sachs analyst Neil Mehta reiterated a buy rating on Chevron with a price target of $241. The analyst is focused on the company's international growth prospects across Latin America, the Middle East, West Africa, and the Eastern Mediterranean.

    Specifically, Mehta highlighted management's commentary on solid execution in Venezuela, with gross production expected to more than double to nearly 600 kbd (kilo barrels per day) by 2031 via three joint ventures. He also noted a recent oil and gas condensate discovery in offshore Angola and is awaiting commercial updates on the West Qurna 2 and Nasiriyah projects in Iraq.

    Recent findings suggest that furthermore, Mehta expects CVX to report improved productivity and capital efficiency across domestic shale assets. He expects the improvement mainly in the Permian Basin, where Chevron projects advanced chemical treatments to drive about a 10% recovery uplift in upcoming wells and bring down capital spend per barrel by about 25% year-over-year. Overall, Mehta expects Chevron to report Q3 2026 EPS of $4.95, above the consensus of $4.89.

    "While unfavorable timing effects and volatile commodity prices may present quarterly earnings headwinds, we highlight healthy U.S. refining margins and strong asset utilization as partial offsets," said Mehta.

    Mehta ranks No. 381 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 12%. See Chevron KPIs on TipRanks.

    Sources indicate that kinetik Holdings (KNTK) is a fully integrated, pure-play, midstream company operating in the Delaware Basin. Earlier this month, the company declared a dividend of $0.81 per share, payable on October 30, 2026. With an annualized dividend of $3.24 per share, KNTK offers a yield of 5.82%. Kinetik will announce its Q3 earnings on November 4, with a conference call scheduled the next day.

    Ahead of Q3 2026 earnings, Goldman Sachs analyst John Mackay reiterated a buy rating on Kinetik stock and slightly raised his price target to $58 from $57. He expects the firm to report Q3 2026 EBITDA of $279 million, higher than the Street's expectation of $270 million but lower than the second quarter's EBITDA of $281 million.

    It has been revealed that the 5-star analyst expects Kinetik's Q3 performance to gain from higher gas volumes after notable curtailments in the second quarter. Mackay also expects the quarter to benefit from higher production and steady commodity margins, even though some lower-margin contracts and weaker Waha spread marketing gains could weigh on results.

    Overall, Mackay increased his Q3 2026 estimates to reflect higher volumes, driven by rapid Permian egress pipeline commissioning, stronger throughput at Kings Landing I, and higher M2M commodity prices, offset by increased costs.

    "As natural gas takeaway constraints ease across the Permian, investor focus centers on KNTK's YE26 volume trajectory and durability of its multi-year growth," noted Mackay.

    Mackay ranks No. 569 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.9%. See Kinetik's Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    Moving to Crescent Energy (CRGY), an exploration and production firm with activities focused in the Eagle Ford, Permian, and Uinta Basins. With a quarterly dividend of $0.12 per share (annualized dividend of $0.48 per share), CRGY's dividend yield stands at 3.56%. Earlier this month, Crescent confirmed an agreement to acquire Eagle Ford assets from Devon Energy (DVN).

    Industry observers note that heading into Q3 earnings on Nov. 2, Evercore analyst Stephen Richardson reiterated a buy rating on Crescent stock and slightly lowered the price target to $17 from $18, citing dilution from new shares.

    "CRGY's recent acquisition of DVN's Eagle Ford assets marks a strategic, growth-oriented move, potentially enhancing cash flow performance," mentioned Richardson.

    Sources indicate that the 5-star analyst noted that the acquisition of the Eagle Ford assets at a net purchase price of $3.85 billion will add about 68 MBoe/d of net production and over 600 net Tier 1 locations. Richardson added that a solid track record of synergies from past deals in the Eagle Ford region increases confidence about Crescent achieving efficiencies with this deal.

    Additionally, Richardson noted that the financial implications of the acquisition seem impressive, with a projected increase in cash flow per share of about 9% for 2027 to 2029.

    The analyst believes that Crescent is not just expanding its business through acquisitions but positioning itself as a more durable tech giant, regardless of market conditions.

    Richardson ranks No. 478 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 63% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Crescent Energy Statistics on TipRanks.

    10 stocks we like better than Global Net Lease ›.

    Industry observers note that on its third-quarter 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 5, 2026, Global Net Lease (GNL -0.17%) raised the lower end of its full-year adjusted funds from operations (AFFO, a real estate cash flow metric) guidance to $0.83 per share. For long-term investors, this focus on disciplined capital allocation helps protect dividend safety and long-term value.

    Three things management noted stand out.

    The manufacturer is selling office properties to eliminate carrying costs and protect straight-line rent, an accounting method that averages lease payments across contract terms. Shifting capital away from office buildings protects cash flow durability across the broader portfolio.

    Sources indicate that low stock prices make issuing latest equity unappealing for funding growth. Instead, management sells noncore assets like gas stations and car washes at favorable capitalization rates (cap rates, the annual return expected from an income property) to repurchase undervalued shares.

    According to recent reports, rising interest rates create headwinds for real estate debt refinancings. Global Net Lease insulated itself by swapping most borrowing to fixed terms, leaving zero debt maturities until late 2027.

    It has been revealed that capital allocation stays disciplined even as borrowing costs remain volatile across commercial real estate markets. The company holds strong liquidity while prioritizing debt reduction and high-return industrial acquisitions.

    Contractual rent increases anchor cash flow durability. The strategy centers on reducing office exposure while using property sales to pay down debt.

    #85554. Breaking: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy Pill Is Capturing 80% of Fresh Oral Obesity Prescriptions. Is NVO Stock a Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (705 w)
    📖 Baca
    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Breaking: Novo Nordisk's Wegovy Pill Is Capturing 80% of Fresh Oral Obesity Prescriptions. Is NVO Stock a Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (705 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.
    • Recent findings suggest that shares of Novo Nordisk (NVO -2.70%) have fallen 70% from the all-time highs reached after it launched the first GLP-1 weight-loss shot.
    • Wall Street may not be giving Novo Nordisk enough credit, especially given the strength of its new GLP-1 pill.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Reuben Gregg Brewer – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:15PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Novo Nordisk ›.

    Recent findings suggest that shares of Novo Nordisk (NVO -2.70%) have fallen 70% from the all-time highs reached after it launched the first GLP-1 weight-loss shot. That has pushed the dividend yield up to 4.5%, well above the pharmaceutical industry average of 1.3%, despite a strong payout ratio of roughly 33%.

    Wall Street may not be giving Novo Nordisk enough credit, especially given the strength of its new GLP-1 pill. Here's why more aggressive investors may want to jump on this high-yield opportunity.

    There's no way to sugarcoat it: Novo Nordisk flubbed the launch of its Wegovy GLP-1 shot. The product was very well received, but the drug maker couldn't keep up with demand. That allowed generics to enter the market early, creating a major competitive headwind. When Eli Lilly (LLY -0.30%) introduced a more effective GLP-1 shot, Novo Nordisk quickly became the number two player. Investors' early enthusiasm quickly turned into deep pessimism.

    That pessimism persists, even after Novo Nordisk's successful launch of a Wegovy pill. Consumers prefer pills over shots, for obvious reasons. That helps explain why Novo Nordisk's pill launch has been even more successful than its GLP-1 shot launch. In fact, in the third quarter, the manufacturer estimates that the Wegovy pill captured eight out of 10 newly introduced patients starting oral GLP-1 weight-loss treatments.

    It has been revealed that the company is executing so well that it increased its full-year 2026 sales and earnings guidance when it reported third-quarter results. From this perspective, Wall Street may be overly negative about the business.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    But there's another problem that investors are grappling with. Novo Nordisk is moving to a volume-driven business model. That involves lowering prices, which has been a headwind for the top and bottom lines. In fact, while the manufacturer updated its guidance, the sales and revenue midpoint is now flat. That's a massive improvement from the previous midpoint of down 3% for both metrics, but it is understandable that investors would remain concerned.

    It has been revealed that essentially, Novo Nordisk needs to prove not only that it remains an innovative drugmaker but also that its volume-driven model is working. And given the intensely competitive healthcare sector, it will likely see additional GLP-1 competition at some point. For example, Pfizer (PFE -0.51%) is hard at work on an acquired long-acting GLP-1 drug it purchased after the tech giant dropped an internal GLP-1 candidate. That said, the global obesity market is very large, so there's likely to be plenty of room for more than one player. And there are also opportunities for companies to fill different niches within the still emerging GLP-1 market.

    In a recent development, for more aggressive dividend investors, the risk/reward balance is likely tilted toward reward with Novo Nordisk. The value opportunity here isn't just highlighted by the lofty yield. The stock's price-to-sales ratio of 3.3x is well below its five-year average of 8x. Its price-to-earnings ratio of roughly 10x is far lower than the five-year average of 23x. And Novo Nordisk's price-to-book ratio of 5.2x is a fraction of its 15x longer-term average. Notably, all of the ratios are lower than they were before the launch of the Wegovy shot. For reference, Eli Lilly's P/E ratio is nearly 45x.

    Given the success Novo Nordisk is seeing with its Wegovy pill and the improved revenue and earnings outlook, it seems like management is executing well as it shifts to a volume-driven model. Add in the lofty yield and attractive valuation, and the story gets even more attractive. If you can handle a little uncertainty, this well-run drug maker is probably worth a very close look right now.

    10 stocks we like better than Dutch Bros ›.

    According to recent reports, long-term investors view broad market sell-offs as offering discounts on growth stocks. That's because, over the long run, stock prices tend to go up. So even amid some general uncertainty now, there could be good deals. Two such stocks we'll look at today are Dutch Bros (BROS -4.01%) and Celsius (CELH -7.36%).

    Recent findings suggest that dutch Bros operates a rapidly expanding network of drive-thru coffee shops, while Celsius markets functional energy drinks through global retail channels. Both companies are disruptors in the competitive beverage stocks landscape. This comparison looks at their growth trajectories and financial health to help you decide which stock fits your strategy.

    It has been revealed that dutch Bros operates a high-growth model focusing on drive-thru shops that serve a variety of hand-crafted beverages. The menu includes coffee, tea, lemonade, and the popular Dutch Bros Rebel energy drink. As of June 2026, the tech giant managed over 1,200 locations in nearly 30 states. Customer concentration is a factor to watch, as the company's brand recognition is somewhat limited.

    Sources indicate that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $2 billion. This represented a revenue growth rate of roughly 30.7% compared to the prior year period. The firm reported a net income of approximately $102 million during this same timeframe. This growth is driven by both upcoming shop openings and steady traffic at existing locations.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Celsius creates and markets functional beverages that have gained significant popularity in the U.S. and international markets. Its portfolio includes brands like CELSIUS and Alani Nu, sold through convenience stores, fitness centers, and large retailers. The tech giant is substantially reliant on PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%) as its primary distributor in the U.S. and Canada. This single customer accounted for over 43% of revenue in 2025, and such high customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue for the tech giant reached roughly $3.2 billion. This reflects significant momentum with revenue growth of approximately 49.1% over the preceding year. During this timeframe, the company generated net income of nearly $230 million.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, dutch Bros faces intense competition from established coffee chains and other quick-service restaurants. Its high geographic concentration in the Western U.S. remains a concern, as most of its shops are located in that region. Rapid expansion also carries risks of identifying suitable real estate and maintaining its unique corporate culture. Regulatory changes regarding labor laws or potential drive-thru bans in specific municipalities could impact its operational model.

    Celsius is heavily dependent on its distribution agreement with Pepsi, which provides the backbone of its retail reach. This relationship creates potential conflicts of interest since Pepsi holds a significant ownership stake and board representation. The tech giant also faces fierce competition from global players such as Monster Beverage (MNST -0.57%) and Red Bull. Additionally, integrating recent acquisitions like Alani Nu and Rockstar presents ongoing execution risks for the management team.

    Celsius appears more attractively valued than Dutch Bros, as it offers a lower earnings multiple despite maintaining a significantly faster revenue growth rate.

    Industry observers note that for investors taking the long view, broad market dips offer buying opportunities. After all, Dutch Bros opened at $35.50 on Nov. 16 and closed at $32.78 on Nov. 20. Celsius also saw its stock price dip, opening at $32.47 on Nov. 16 and closing at $28.46 by Nov. 20.

    Choosing between the two growth stocks for a portfolio, however, I would rather own Dutch Bros.

    One of the key reasons is that, as a growth stock, Celsius appears to be increasingly relying on acquisitions. In the third quarter of 2026, revenue for its CELSIUS brand fell by approximately 6%, and U.S. retail sales fell by 7%. It saw strong growth through its acquired Alani Nu brand, with revenue climbing 24% and retail sales growing 57.9%.

    In a recent development, in comparison, in its third quarter, Dutch Bros grew revenue by nearly 30%, same-shop sales increased by 5.4%, and customer traffic grew by 1%. Granted, it's not an apples-to-apples comparison, given the differences in how the businesses operate. Still, it reveals that the growth opportunities for Dutch Bros come through its core offerings, as its stores are attracting more customers, selling more, and have future sales growth opportunities through latest store openings.

    While Celsius is buying growth, Dutch Bros is creating it. That makes Dutch Bros the stock I would want to buy for the long term, using sell-offs to pick up shares at a discount to where they could be trading in the future.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:18PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Kraft Heinz ›.

    It has been revealed that should everyday investors favor a turnaround value play or a reliable beverage leader? This match-up explores whether Kraft Heinz (KHC +1.89%) or Coca-Cola (KO +0.94%) is the better buy for your portfolio heading into 2027.

    Recent findings suggest that kraft Heinz focuses on household food staples and condiments, while Coca-Cola dominates the global non-alcoholic beverage market. Both companies provide essential products that often resist economic downturns, yet they follow very different growth paths and valuation models today. This comparison breaks down their latest financial results and potential risks to help you make an informed decision.

    According to recent reports, kraft Heinz produces and markets a massive global portfolio of branded foods and condiments, ranging from its namesake ketchup to Philadelphia cream cheese. As one of the prominent consumer staples stocks, it sells its products in more than 40 countries through retail and foodservice channels. Its largest customer is Walmart (WMT +1.51%), which accounts for approximately 21% of net sales, and this customer concentration adds a layer of risk to the business.

    It has been revealed that in the 12 months ended Sept. 26, 2026, revenue reached nearly $24.8 billion, representing a slight decline of approximately 1.5% compared to the prior period. The company reported a net loss of roughly $3.5 billion during this timeframe, and its net margin was approximately -14%. These results reflect a period of adjustment as the company manages its global portfolio and navigates changing retail demand.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Coca-Cola is a global beverage powerhouse that owns or licenses hundreds of brands across categories like sparkling soft drinks, sports drinks, and juices. The organization utilizes a vast network of independent bottling partners, including Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (CCEP +0.72%) and Coca-Cola HBC (CCHBF +0.67%), to distribute its products in over 200 countries. It recently secured an exclusive pouring rights agreement with KFC U.S. starting in January 2027.

    In the 12 months ended Oct. 2, 2026, revenue reached approximately $51.1 billion, which represents a healthy growth of roughly 7.1% over the prior year. The organization delivered net income of $14.6 billion, resulting in a strong net margin of about 28.7%. This profitability highlights the strength of its brands and its ability to maintain pricing power in various global markets.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Kraft Heinz faces intense competition from both major branded rivals, such as PepsiCo (PEP +1.11%) and Nestlé (NSRGF +1.24%), and low-cost private-label products. The organization must constantly adapt to rapidly changing consumer preferences and is dependent on key retail customers, who may reduce shelf space or pricing leverage. Additionally, supply chain volatility and potential future impairments of its intangible assets remain significant concerns for the business.

    According to recent reports, coca-Cola is exposed to risks from unfavorable global economic and geopolitical conditions that can impact its international operations. The manufacturer also faces health-related concerns regarding sweetened beverages, which often lead to increased regulatory scrutiny and shifts in consumer habits. Furthermore, Coca-Cola depends heavily on independent bottling partners and must navigate challenges like water scarcity and maintaining its brand image in a competitive landscape against PepsiCo and Keurig Dr Pepper (KDP +1.25%).

    Kraft Heinz at the moment looks cheaper based on its much lower forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and price-to-sales (P/S) ratio, suggesting it is priced as a value stock compared to Coca-Cola.

    In a recent development, between the two, I favor Coca-Cola more for a simple reason: Kraft Heinz is executing a turnaround, while Coca-Cola is just executing.Looking at its recent performance for the third quarter of 2026, unit case volume grew 5%, organic revenue grew 7%, comparable earnings per share (EPS) grew 11%, and operating income grew 12%. Overall, that highlights not only consumers buying more, but also Coca-Cola converting demand for its products into greater profits.

    Also promising in those quarterly results was that volume growth wasn't tied to just one geographic area, giving Coca-Cola multiple markets and helping reduce reliance on just one market.

    Recent findings suggest that in addition, it's seeing success with its classic offerings, with Coca-Cola volume growing 5% in that quarter. But it's also seeing even larger volume growth with tweaks to its classic formulas, with Coca-Cola Zero Sugar volume growing 16%. To finish out the year, Coca-Cola's management expects 5% organic revenue growth and 11% comparable EPS growth.

    While Kraft Heinz needs to show investors it can earn their confidence back, Coca-Cola has already earned the confidence. It just needs to keep executing from here.

    Industry News: Robinhood shares fall as crypto slump weighs on profits, offsetting gains in fresh businesses

    📅 27 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (336 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.
    • Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept.
    • Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Robinhood shares were down around 8% in pre-market trading on Wednesday as investors digested weaker-than-expected third-quarter earnings despite growth in options trading and prediction markets.

    Here's how the brokerage performed in its quarter ended Sept. 30, compared with Wall Street estimates, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:.

    Robinhood's net income fell to $468 million, or 51 cents per share, from $556 million, or 61 cents per share, a year ago. Revenue represented a 12% increase from $1.27 billion in the same quarter last year.

    Despite that gain, transaction-based revenue of $867 million came in below Wall Street estimates from StreetAccount of $879 million, putting focus on whether Robinhood can sustain momentum across its trading businesses and reduce its reliance on volatile market activity.

    Recent findings suggest that robinhood has been diversifying its business as it tries to expand its brokerage app into a broader financial services platform. Options trading and event contracts have become increasingly key sources of transaction revenue, while the manufacturer has continued to invest in wealth management, subscriptions and other offerings.

    Transaction-based revenue grew 19% from the same period last year to $867 million, driven primarily by a more than 500% increase in event contracts revenue. Additionally, options revenue grew 31% to $399 million and equities revenue rose 41% to $121 million.

    Those gains were partially offset by cryptocurrency revenue, which fell 55% to $120 million.

    Chief Financial Officer Shiv Verma told CNBC event contracts on crypto movements did well in the quarter, offering investors another way to express a view on crypto despite the slump in prices and spot trading.

    Recent findings suggest that net deposits on the Robinhood platform totaled $15.7 billion for the quarter, equal to a 17% annualized growth rate based on total platform assets at the end of Q2 2026. Over the past year, net deposits totaled $71 billion, representing 21% growth compared with total platform assets at the end of Q3 2025.

    —With reporting from CNBC's Robert Hum and Kate Rooney.

    Business & Policy ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Oklo vs. NuScale Power: Which Nuclear Stock Is a Better Buy?

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (779 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:19PM EST.
    • As data centers hunt for power, Oklo (OKLO -4.75%) and NuScale Power (SMR -11.81%) have emerged as two of the most prominent contenders in the nuclear space.
    • According to recent reports, both companies aim to build smaller reactors that can sit closer to the point of use.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:19PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Oklo ›.

    As data centers hunt for power, Oklo (OKLO -4.75%) and NuScale Power (SMR -11.81%) have emerged as two of the most prominent contenders in the nuclear space.

    According to recent reports, both companies aim to build smaller reactors that can sit closer to the point of use. Oklo emphasizes fuel recycling and has unique partnerships, while NuScale focuses on a modular design already certified by federal regulators.

    In a recent development, oklo designs fast-fission power plants intended to serve specialized customers like data centers, industrial factories, and military installations. The organization is right now targeting major players like Meta Platforms (META -5.93%), Equinix (EQIX -4.89%), and Diamondback Energy (FANG -0.58%) for long-term power agreements. Because its business model revolves around a few massive potential contracts, customer concentration adds a significant layer of risk to the enterprise.

    Oklo does not yet report meaningful revenue, as it has not yet brought its first powerhouses online. As of Sept. 30, it had total cash, cash equivalents, and debt securities of $3.1 billion. For the first nine months of 2026, it recorded a net loss of $123.3 million.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Sources indicate that nuScale Power focuses on small modular reactors designed to be safer and easier to deploy than traditional large-scale nuclear plants. The tech giant relies heavily on an exclusive strategic partnership with ENTRA1 for global sales and development. Key collaborations include work with the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVC +0.17%) and other project engagements.

    In a recent development, like Oklo, NuScale does not report meaningful revenue. It ended the third quarter of 2026 with $1.9 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and investments. For the first nine months of 2026, its net loss sits at $135.2 million.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    In a recent development, oklo faces significant risks due to its lack of commercial operating history and the absence of binding power purchase agreements. The tech giant is developing first-of-a-kind technology that requires complex regulatory approval from both the Nuclear Regulatory Commission and the Department of Energy. Furthermore, securing a scalable supply of specialized nuclear fuel remains a major hurdle for its future growth and operational success.

    It has been revealed that nuScale Power faces substantial risks related to ongoing securities class action litigation involving its disclosures about project prospects and competitive advantages. The business depends almost entirely on its partnership with ENTRA1, and any termination of that agreement could be devastating for its commercialization efforts. NuScale may still need to secure significant future capital to reach its commercial delivery targets.

    As neither organization generates meaningful revenue nor is profitable, it is difficult to rely solely on traditional metrics to make an investment decision.

    I could see the case for adding both Oklo and NuScale to a portfolio. That way, you can still make money from the upside of the nuclear energy market while not being tied to the success of either company. Still, between the two, I would rather own Oklo because of its unique setup. NuScale's success will primarily depend on selling its reactors, while Oklo has multiple revenue stream opportunities it can eventually tap into.

    Sources indicate that it's a unique business model in that it attempts to develop reactors, sell energy and heat, recycle fuel, and engage in isotope production simultaneously. That does introduce more execution risk, trying to achieve multiple objectives at once, and it also makes it difficult to estimate the future value of what all that would look like when it's up and running. But the main takeaway is that, because of those opportunities, its sales-generating potential could be greater than that of other nuclear players.

    In a recent development, as mentioned earlier, Oklo already has some buy-in from big names, such as Meta Platforms. Oklo intends to develop a 1.2 GW power campus in Ohio that will support Meta's data centers in the region, and the agreement allows Meta to prepay for power and offer funding to advance the project.

    What Oklo could fully accomplish is still years away from fruition, so this should remain a small, speculative position in a portfolio.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:20PM EST.
    • Choosing between Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) and Uber Technologies (UBER -3.25%) involves weighing two different tech stocks.
    • Shopify acts as the digital backbone for millions of online merchants, while Uber manages a massive logistics and transportation network.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Jack Delaney – Updated Nov 21, 2026 at 5:20PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than Shopify ›.

    Choosing between Shopify (SHOP -6.25%) and Uber Technologies (UBER -3.25%) involves weighing two different tech stocks. Both companies have become essential to how we shop and move.

    Shopify acts as the digital backbone for millions of online merchants, while Uber manages a massive logistics and transportation network. This comparison evaluates their financials and business models to see which is a better pick for 2027 and beyond.

    Sources indicate that shopify provides the essential digital tools that allow companies to build their own online storefronts and manage physical retail locations. The company serves millions of merchants in multiple countries, providing an all-in-one ecosystem for everything from inventory management to payment processing. By focusing on giving brands total control over their customer relationships, it has become a central player among tech stocks that support the broader e-commerce market.

    In a recent development, in the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $14.2 billion, representing an increase of approximately 32.5% compared to the prior twelve-month period. This robust growth was accompanied by net income of $2.1 billion.

    NASDAQ · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    Uber Technologies operates a massive technology platform that connects people to transportation, food delivery, and logistics services. Its network spans over 70 countries, serving a growing number of monthly active consumers who use the app for ridesharing or ordering from local merchants. The firm leverages partnerships with major retailers like Best Buy (BBY -1.33%) and Tractor Supply (TSCO -0.77%) to expand its reach beyond traditional restaurant delivery into a broader marketplace.

    In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached nearly $56.5 billion, which is a growth rate of approximately 13.9% over the previous twelve months. The firm generated net income of around $3.5 billion during this period.

    NYSE · As of 4:00 PM ET 11/20/26.

    It has been revealed that shopify faces intense market competition from established platforms and niche providers that could limit its growth or force pricing changes. The company depends heavily on third-party cloud infrastructure from Alphabet (GOOGL -2.70%) and payment processors like PayPal Holdings (PYPL -5.46%). Newly introduced risks involve the use of artificial intelligence, which could lead to inaccurate outputs or regulatory challenges.

    Recent findings suggest that uber Technologies deals with ongoing legal and regulatory challenges regarding how it classifies its drivers, which could fundamentally change its business model. It competes globally in mobility and delivery against well-capitalized rivals such as Lyft (LYFT -2.54%) and DoorDash (DASH -2.88%). The platform is also vulnerable to macroeconomic shifts, as inflation or rising fuel prices can impact consumer spending on rides and deliveries. Finally, the organization relies on the mobile marketplaces of Apple (AAPL -1.90%) and Alphabet to reach its vast user base.

    Uber Technologies appears more reasonably priced as it trades at a much lower forward price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio and price-to-sales (P/S) ratio than Shopify.

    Both are well-run companies. But if I had to pick only one stock, it would be Uber. It's not so much about anything Shopify is doing wrong; it's more about Uber growing its current business and the opportunities ahead.

    Industry observers note that despite Uber being a well-established brand, its recent 2026 third-quarter earnings results showed that monthly active users increased by 14% to 215 million. Trips also increased by 16% to 4.1 billion, and gross bookings climbed 20% to roughly $60 billion. That shows not only that more people are signing up to use its platform, but that users are also booking more rides and deliveries.

    In a recent development, for its sales growth opportunities, the focus should be on robotaxis, which could be a huge market. According to research from Goldman Sachs (GS -6.71%), the global robotaxi market size is expected to reach $415 billion by 2035. By the end of 2026, Uber expects to have 700 fully driverless vehicles on its platform, with more than 2,000 in 2027.

    Sources indicate that shopify will continue to benefit from the growth of e-commerce sales. But for long-term investors, understanding that the roads over the next decade will be filled with more autonomous vehicles, Uber can be a centerpiece in that market, which should only grow in value.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (681 w)

    General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Fool ↗ Open Full Page

    Latest Update: In the Last Tech Bust, the S&P 500 Lost Money for a Decade. History Notes Stocks With the Highest Yields Gained 5.4% a Year.

    📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (681 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Fool

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • It has been revealed that the AI trade seems to be unwinding fast.
    • Industry observers note that however, history offers a useful reference for what held up the last time a technology boom ended.
    • Industry observers note that the dot-com bubble burst in March 2000.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    By Matt DiLallo – Nov 21, 2026 at 5:31PM EST.

    10 stocks we like better than S&P 500 Index ›.

    It has been revealed that the AI trade seems to be unwinding fast. The Nasdaq Composite (^IXIC -5.28%) was recently down more than 15% from its early October peak, while the S&P 500 (^GSPC -3.70%) was approaching correction territory, with a roughly 10% slump from its all-time high. Nobody knows how this downturn will play out.

    Industry observers note that however, history offers a useful reference for what held up the last time a technology boom ended. From 2000 to 2009, a period that featured the dot-com crash, the S&P 500 posted negative returns, averaging a 0.8% annual decline. High-yielding dividend stocks, on the other hand, delivered an average annual total return of 5.4% over the same period, according to a Wellington Management study published by Hartford Funds. Here's what investors can learn from this history lesson.

    Industry observers note that the dot-com bubble burst in March 2000. It led many stock investors to return to fundamentals, focusing on metrics such as a manufacturer's price-to-earnings ratio and dividend yield instead of future monetization potential. Companies that generated real revenue and profits, and returned a portion of their income to investors via dividends, delivered the best returns during this period.

    Wellington sorted dividend-paying stocks into five groups by yield, from the top 20% of payers to the bottom 20%. In the 2000s, the highest-yielding group gained 5.4% a year, while the lowest-yielding payers lost 1.7% a year. To put this in dollars, $1,000 compounding at 5.4% for 10 years grows to about $1,690, while $1,000 shrinking at 0.8% per year ends up near $923.

    The decade before the dot-com bust looked very different for high-yielding dividend stocks. In the 1990s, the lowest-yielding payers kept pace with the S&P 500, while the highest-yielding group trailed it by a meaningful amount. Meanwhile, the last six years look a lot like the late 1990s. Since 2020, the lowest-yielding payers have beaten the market, while the highest-yielding group has trailed.

    Sources indicate that the highest-yielding dividend stocks have outperformed the market in five of 10 time periods from 1930 to 2025. That's the same percentage as the lowest yielders. The best performers were companies with higher dividend yields, though not the highest. These companies prioritized dividend payments (and growth) without sacrificing financial flexibility. This cohort outperformed the S&P 500 in six of those 10 periods, including in the 2000s (4.4% annualized return). They also delivered solid performance leading up to the dot-com crash (15.6% returns in the 1990s).

    Here are three practical tips investors can employ in their own portfolios based on the data on dividend stocks:.

    A high yield can be as much a warning as a reward. A stock's yield rises when its price falls, and sometimes the market is pricing in a dividend cut. The data on cutters show how costly that can be. From 1973 through 2025, S&P 500 companies that cut or eliminated their dividends returned an average of -1% a year, compared with 10.2% for companies that raised theirs and 7.7% for the average stock, according to Ned Davis Research data published by Hartford. Cutters were also the most volatile group.

    It has been revealed that the last time a technology boom ended, the stocks that paid the most were the ones that held up best, while the lowest-yielding payers lost more than the market. That doesn't mean history will repeat itself, and the biggest yields carry their own risks, as dividend cutters show. However, the data makes a case for adding some yield to your portfolio before the next cycle turns.

    Industry observers note that on its third quarter of 2026 earnings call, held on Nov. 16, 2026, iQiyi (IQ -10.96%) announced that content costs declined as it returned to non-GAAP (adjusted accounting) operating profit. The streaming platform is shifting toward artificial intelligence production and decentralized content sharing to lower upfront financial risk. Three takeaways from the call highlight this strategic pivot.

    Shifting content creation toward revenue sharing allows third-party creators to absorb production costs while iQiyi pays based on viewer performance. This model lowers fixed cash outlays and reduces the platform's dependence on unpredictable blockbuster releases.

    It has been revealed that deploying AIGC (artificial intelligence-generated content) helps the platform turn existing IP (intellectual property) into commercial projects much faster. The three chapters of The Ferry Man series each recouped their entire budget during their first week online.

    According to recent reports, short-form dramas--episodes running 15 to 30 minutes--offer quick production turns and lower risk than traditional serialized shows. iQiyi captured the top market share in this fast-growing category during the quarter.

    It has been revealed that content costs are falling while the platform builds dedicated online creator tools and expands connected television advertising. Management is strengthening its subscription service and creator network while using artificial intelligence to accelerate output.

    By focusing on disciplined investments and expanding revenue-sharing models, management aims to turn efficiency gains into consistent long-term cash flow.

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers.
    • In this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income.
    • Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Democrats' midterm election win has put the artificial intelligence trade in question, as voters clearly expressed opposition to the rapid buildout of data centers. The stock market could remain volatile amid AI trade concerns, macro uncertainties, and geopolitical tensions.

    In this scenario, investors can add dividend-paying stocks to their portfolios to earn steady income. However, the extensive universe of dividend stocks can make selection challenging. Top Wall Street analysts' recommendations can help investors shortlist attractive dividend stocks, as these experts assign ratings after in-depth financial analysis.

    Here are three dividend-paying stocks that are highlighted by Wall Street's top pros, as tracked by TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

    Industry observers note that viper Energy (VNOM) is a subsidiary of Diamondback and owns and acquires mineral and royalty interests, primarily in the Permian Basin. The manufacturer reported upbeat third-quarter earnings, supported by recent acquisitions and continued development activity from Diamondback and third-party operators. Viper unveiled a base cash dividend of 50 cents per share for Q3 2026, payable on Nov. 19. Based on the base and variable dividends announced over the past 12 months, VNOM's dividend yield stands at 5.7%.

    Following the Q3 results, TD Cowen analyst Aaron Bilkoski reiterated a buy rating on Viper Energy stock with a price target of $61. The analyst noted that the organization delivered solid Q3 results, with production, including oil and natural gas liquids, exceeding both TD Cowen and consensus estimates.

    The 5-star analyst highlighted that the key update was the announcement of two royalty acquisitions for $809 million in cash, including deferred consideration, and $82 million of newly issued shares.

    Given the recently revealed base dividend hike, Bilkoski expects Viper to direct incremental free cash flow toward buybacks. While the acquisitions increase leverage, the analyst believes that Viper has enough capacity for opportunistic buybacks.

    In a recent development, bilkoski noted that Viper has historically delivered one of the highest production per share growth profiles in his royalty coverage, but still trades at a notable discount to the royalty peer average and the company's historical FCF yield range. "In our view, its above-average growth warrants a higher valuation," mentioned the analyst.

    Bilkoski ranks No. 525 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 12.80%. See Viper Energy Stock Buybacks on TipRanks.

    Exxon Mobil (XOM) reported robust Q3 2026 profits, as its U.S. refineries boosted production to capitalize on the high diesel fuel prices sparked by the conflict in the Middle East. The oil and gas giant revealed a quarterly dividend of $1.07 per share, payable on Dec. 10, reflecting a 3.9% increase. This marks Exxon's 44th consecutive year of dividend increases. At an annualized dividend of $4.28 per share, XOM offers a yield of 2.53%.

    Impressed by the Q3 print, TD Cowen analyst Jason Gabelman reiterated a buy rating on Exxon stock and raised his price target to $193 from $180 to reflect higher downstream earnings, with the expectation of increased mid-cycle margins.

    Industry observers note that gabelman noted that the strength in Exxon's refining business continues to offset Middle East-related headwinds. He added that the firm increased its ownership in LNG projects, which should reduce its Middle East concentration over time from 75% to 50% and lower the likelihood of diversification-focused mergers and acquisitions. Beyond LNG, Gabelman expects Exxon's growth in the 2030s to come from Guyana, Kashagan, Permian, and possibly Venezuela.

    Gabelman noted that Exxon confirmed a dividend hike of nearly 4% and looks to maintain buybacks at $20 billion for 2027. "The decision to maintain reduces the pro-cyclicality nature of the buyback," stated the analyst.

    Gabelman ranks No. 347 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 16.90%. See Exxon Mobil Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

    According to recent reports, williams (WMB), which owns and operates energy infrastructure to deliver natural gas, reported strong third-quarter results. The company announced a quarterly dividend of $0.525 per share, or $2.10 per share annualized, payable on Dec. 28. WMB offers a dividend yield of 3.09%.

    In reaction to the Q3 2026 results, CIBC analyst Robert Catellier reaffirmed a buy rating on Williams stock with a price target of $82. The analyst noted that Q3 results were essentially in line with expectations and reflected continued strength in execution across WMB's infrastructure portfolio.

    Catellier stated that Williams' Q3 performance was driven by higher transmission, storage, and power generation revenues, as well as contributions from the Momentum Midstream acquisition.

    Industry observers note that he noted that Williams maintained its full-year EBITDA guidance of $8.3 billion to $8.5 billion. In fact, results are tracking toward the higher end of the guidance range, backed by contributions from recently completed projects and the Momentum Midstream deal. WMB continues to target long-term EBITDA compound annual growth rate of at least 11% through 2030.

    Catellier expects WMB's long-term targets to be supported by incremental transmission and storage opportunities, including Transco's Southeast Supply Enhancement II project and an 84 MMcf/d expansion of the Garden Connector project.

    It has been revealed that catellier ranks No. 667 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 66% of the time, delivering an average return of 9.60%. See Williams Technical Analysis on TipRanks.

    • The artificial intelligence organization raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.
    • Recent findings suggest that anthropic said it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Anthropic underwriters have officially exercised their overallotment of shares in the historic initial public offering, bringing the total raised to $93.5 billion, according to a release Friday.

    The artificial intelligence organization raised $81.3 billion on Wednesday and netted an additional $12.2 billion through the overallotment, surpassing SpaceX, which held a record IPO in June.

    Recent findings suggest that anthropic said it sold an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at $83 per share in the offering. It sold 980 million shares on Wednesday and its underwriters had the option to purchase up to an additional 147 million shares by Friday as part of the overallotment, which is commonly referred to as the "greenshoe.".

    Sources indicate that shares of the Claude maker opened trading at $111.50 on the Nasdaq on Thursday, but slid throughout the day and closed at $97.17. The stock sank 12% in premarket trading on Friday during a broad tech sell-off.

    According to recent reports, in addition to the sale of its Class A common stock, Anthropic closed a concurrent sale of its Class N common stock after a group of tech companies, including Advanced Micro Devices, Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and others, agreed to participate in a $26 billion private placement at the IPO price. Anthropic remarked Friday that aggregate gross proceeds from its IPO, including the private placement, totaled $119.5 billion, before deducting offering expenses.

    Anthropic dodged an unforgiving series of obstacles on its road to the Nasdaq on Thursday, as investors brooded over Jensen Huang's shocking ouster at Nvidia, voters' stinging rebuke of the tech during the midterms and whether rising interest rates would stymie industry plans for a multitrillion-dollar AI infrastructure buildout.

    CEO Dario Amodei co-founded the tech giant in 2021 after he and a handful of other researchers, including his sister Daniela, quit their jobs at OpenAI, now Anthropic's chief rival. Anthropic is best known for developing a family of AI models called Claude, which have captivated the corporate world and fueled the company's historic rise.

    The siblings celebrated the IPO as a "milestone" in an interview with CNBC on Thursday, but mentioned there's more work ahead for Anthropic.

    "For us, it's like one stop on the journey," Daniela Amodei noted. "We think about this as, 'Wow, this is an incredible moment for Anthropic for our mission, but we're going to wake up tomorrow and we're going to be the same firm.'".

    Trump says he discussed Jensen Huang with Xi; Bessent tells CNBC Nvidia chip export policy is unchanged

    📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (884 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

    ⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • According to recent reports, president Donald Trump on Friday remarked he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week.
    • Sources indicate that "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he stated, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant!
    • Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent remarked "no," without elaborating.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    According to recent reports, president Donald Trump on Friday remarked he and Chinese leader Xi Jinping discussed their shared affinity for former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang during their talks in China this week. Earlier in the day, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the ousted leader was not mentioned in separate talks he had with Chinese officials.

    Sources indicate that "I did discuss that with President Xi, and he stated, 'Oh, brilliant, brilliant! He's a brilliant man.' He is," Trump said at a White House press conference.

    Asked earlier Friday on CNBC's "Squawk on the Street" if Huang, a close ally of Trump's, had come up in "any of your discussions with the Chinese," Bessent remarked "no," without elaborating.

    A senior Trump administration official later mentioned that both Trump's and Bessent's remarks were correct, and that both were addressing their own conversations. The official spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss those conversations.

    Trump also reiterated that he would like to see Huang — who was replaced by interim CEO Colette Kress after resigning amid allegations of an extramarital affair with a Chinese spy — be restored as Nvidia's CEO.

    Industry observers note that "I would love to see Jensen be given a second chance," Trump stated. "You know, we're a country of second chances, and I'd love to be able to see him. That's a very important firm to us, and he put us in a position where we are literally 10 years advanced over other companies.".

    Nvidia's board is not considering bringing Huang back, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC earlier this week.

    Sources indicate that the president's comments came amid growing scrutiny of advanced U.S. chips, including those made by Nvidia, ending up in China either legally or by being diverted via third countries.

    Both Trump's and Bessent's remarks are potentially an indication that the Trump administration may not focus on cracking down on China's efforts to acquire advanced chips.

    Bessent suggested that U.S. policy allowing the sale of Nvidia's powerful H200 AI chips to China remains unchanged following the talks in Shenzhen this week.

    According to recent reports, "We've already agreed that the ... H200s are the threshold level of chips that could be sold to the Chinese, and, you know, that continues as planned," Bessent remarked.

    "I wouldn't anticipate any change in the policy," he added after CNBC's Sara Eisen noted that Nvidia stated it had stopped selling H200s to China.

    Recent findings suggest that the administration ignoring the subject of Huang's affair with a possible Chinese spy — whose Singapore-based company Megaspeed has been accused of acting as a cutout for Beijing — contrasts with the importance Trump has placed on beating China in the race to artificial intelligence dominance. It could suggest that despite his support for the U.S. AI industry, Trump is less concerned with addressing China's ongoing efforts to acquire U.S. semiconductors.

    It has been revealed that trump has also defended Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who has come under fire from multiple directions for reportedly slow-walking export restrictions on Chinese chip sales. "I understand both sides of it," Trump said on Monday when he also said he's like to see Huang back as CEO.

    Bessent's appearance on CNBC came after Trump's return from a tour through Asia that saw him meet with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen, China.

    The meeting was historic as the first time the leaders of the three countries had met without other nations' counterparts. But the trilateral summit appeared to yield few deliverables on any number of the most pressing global issues related to the countries, including the Ukraine and Iran wars or the ongoing AI race.

    Bessent told CNBC on Friday that there was a "robust discussion" between Trump and Xi on trade policy and AI.

    They "agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions," he noted, abbreviating the term "super intelligence," Trump's attempted rebrand of AI.

    In a CNBC appearance last week, Bessent lamented the "leakage" of U.S.-made AI chips to China and blamed the Commerce Department, led by Lutnick, for slow-walking export controls on suspected Chinese cutouts like Megaspeed.

    Multiple Trump administration leaders have long sought to impose export restrictions on Megaspeed, but Commerce "has the pen" and "you will have to ask them about their internal processes," Bessent said in that interview.

    On Friday, however, Bessent was much more tight-lipped.

    Sources indicate that asked if there is a dispute between him and Lutnick over how aggressively the U.S. should be pursuing Chinese export controls, Bessent said, "I think we're all committed to following President Trump's instructions.".

    Sources indicate that "I think we are going to see that the ... proper chip restrictions are in place, and the remote access has been curtailed," he added. Commerce recently took steps to close one of China's paths to accessing AI processors.

    Correction: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent spoke to CNBC's "Squawk on the Street." A previous version of this story misstated the name of the show.

    Editor's note: This story and headline have been updated following additional information provided by the Trump administration about the nature of Bessent's and Trump's meetings in China.

    • Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
    • In a recent development, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure.
    • The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.

    In a recent development, miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.

    The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.

    Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.

    It has been revealed that securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo stated. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters.".

    Industry observers note that securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The firm posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.

    Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and unveiled the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.

    Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo noted.The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.

    "We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth.".
